| [NOTE-428](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-428.md) | How effective psychological treatments work: mechanisms of change in cognitive behavioural therapy and beyond | A history-and-argument paper. It separates common factors from mechanisms of change, holds that a treatment's success does not validate its theory, and proposes one mechanism for all effective therapy: the person, "stuck" in an exaggerated negative meaning (Theory A) maintained by their own reactions, builds and tests a less threatening alternative (Theory B), a meaning-making flexibility. | [NOTE-429](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-429.md) | The Emerging Field of Emotion Regulation: An Integrative Review | Gross's founding review. Emotions are modulable response tendencies. Regulation, defined as influencing which emotions one has, when, and how they are experienced and expressed, is split from coping, mood regulation and defense, and sorted into five families by where it acts in emotion generation: situation selection, situation modification, attentional deployment, cognitive change, response modulation. The paper's own open problem is whether regulation can be told apart from generation at all. | Read |
| [NOTE-430](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-430.md) | Relational Frame Theory: Some Implications for Understanding and Treating Human Psychopathology | RFT stated for clinicians. Human relating is bidirectional and arbitrarily applicable, a generalized operant under contextual control, with mutual and combinatorial entailment and transformation of function. Relating relations explains metaphor, rules are networks whose coordination with events regulates behaviour, and the self is content, process and context. These are offered as the reason direct-contingency behaviour therapy is "inadequate", and ACT's acceptance, defusion and values are given RFT readings explicitly labelled heuristic. | Read |
| [NOTE-431](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-431.md) | Acceptance and Commitment Therapy: Model, Processes and Outcomes | The ACT model, read in an early manuscript. Psychopathology is psychological inflexibility: cognitive fusion (fed by literality, reason-giving and emotional control) supports experiential avoidance, and both displace present-moment contact and values. Six processes restore flexibility. The manuscript's evidence: AAQ correlations with distress (21 studies), component studies of acceptance and defusion, mediation in seven trials, and weighted outcome effect sizes (d = .49 post and .69 follow-up against active treatments). | Read |
| [NOTE-432](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-432.md) | Explanatory Models for Psychiatric Illness | Psychiatric etiology is multilevel, non-aggregative and full of causal loops, so law-based explanation fails and so do both hard reduction and hard emergence. Mechanistic explanation proceeds by local decomposition and difficult reassembly. Following Marr, biology implements the functions psychology describes and does not replace them. | [NOTE-435](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-435.md) | A Network Theory of Mental Disorders | Borsboom states the network theory as five principles: complexity, symptom-component correspondence, direct causal connections between symptoms, disorders as tightly coupled symptom clusters, and hysteresis. Disorder is an alternative stable state of a strongly connected network that outlasts its trigger; health is the stable state of a weakly connected one. | [NOTE-436](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-436.md) | Psychological Flexibility as a Fundamental Aspect of Health | A narrative review that defines psychological flexibility by four dynamic abilities (adapting to situations, reconfiguring resources, shifting perspective, balancing domains). It recommends experience sampling and multi-informant measures over global self-report. | Read |
| [NOTE-437](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-437.md) | The Future of Intervention Science: Process-Based Therapy | A programme paper. Thirty years of DSM-linked trials never turned syndromes into diseases, so evidence-based therapy should target theory-derived, empirically supported processes of change with procedures shown to move them. Its distinctive commitments are a falsification rule for models of change, moderated mediation as a basis for a new nosology, and an idiographic, functional-analytic diagnosis. It offers predictions and cited examples, not new data. | Read |
